memory_candidates: A verified-prototype-to-module transcription can be a zero-fix promotion when the source already compiles under a lean_lib carrying identical leanOptions -- checking option parity between the probe's library and the target library before dispatch predicted the outcome exactly.

lake-build-guard.sh build takes the full lake subcommand after `--`: `-- build TARGET`, not `-- TARGET`. Passing a bare target yields `error: unknown command '<target>'` while the guard still exits 0, so a caller that trusts the exit code alone will read a failed build as a pass.

When a build warning is flagged against new work, check whether Lake reported the emitting module as 'Replayed' rather than 'Built': a replayed module's diagnostics come from cache and its build inputs are unchanged, which combined with a clean `git status` on that file is sufficient to attribute the warning to pre-existing code.
